verdict.rationale: Clerk documents webhooks that deliver event notifications, such as when a user is created or updated. That is a developer building block: the user must build their own handler to act on the event. The evidence shows no first-party way to define rules that automatically trigger actions on events. Sign-up limits and allow/block lists are adjacent access controls, not event-triggered automation rules.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
